title: Training Dense Retrievers with Multiple Positive Passages

problem.claim: Retriever training relies on sparse single-positive annotations that introduce false-negative noise and suboptimal supervision.

gap.claim: The optimal way to incorporate large-scale multi-positive relevance signals into retriever training is poorly understood.

contributions.claim: A systematic study of multi-positive optimization objectives for retriever training.
Representative multi-positive objectives are unified under a shared contrastive learning framework.
The objectives are theoretically characterized by their distinct gradient behaviors and probability-mass allocation across positive document sets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive evaluations were conducted on Natural Questions, MS~MARCO, and BEIR in homogeneous LLM-annotated and heterogeneous human-plus-LLM label regimes.
LSEPair reportedly achieved superior robustness and performance across the evaluated settings, while JointLH and SumMargLH were sensitive to positive-label quality.
Rand1LH reportedly served as a reliable baseline.

narrative_sequence.summary: Effective retrievers establish the performance ceiling for downstream knowledge-intensive systems.
Sparse single-positive annotations create false-negative noise and weak supervision, while the best use of dense relevance labels remains unclear.
The study compares and unifies multi-positive objectives and analyzes their gradient behavior.
Experiments evaluate the objectives across datasets and homogeneous or heterogeneous labeling regimes.
LSEPair is reported as the most robust and effective objective, with Rand1LH as a reliable baseline.

source_observation.claim: LSEPair reportedly performs robustly across homogeneous and heterogeneous positive-label regimes.

interpretation.claim: An objective that is less sensitive to positive-label quality may be preferable when supervision sources vary.

application.claim: When training with mixed human and LLM relevance labels, evaluate LSEPair alongside simpler baselines.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that LSEPair is optimal outside the evaluated datasets, regimes, or implementation conditions.

source_observation.claim: Rand1LH is reported as a reliable baseline.

interpretation.claim: Simple sampling-based objectives can provide a useful reference point for dense-supervision methods.

application.claim: Include Rand1LH as a baseline when comparing multi-positive retriever objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when Rand1LH may outperform the other objectives or how reliability was measured.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify model architectures, training hyperparameters, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not report numerical results or statistical significance.
The abstract does not describe how LLM-annotated relevance labels were generated or validated.
